name: Nettle Plant
location: Small groups in shaded forest rough, away from the walking line.
fit: Serrated leaves and visible veins add close-up botanical detail.
caveat: Keep sparse and outside maintained turf; use as wild foliage, not a hazard mechanic.

name: Periwinkle Plant
location: A few pink-flowering patches along the forest-to-beach discovery path.
fit: Echoes the pink trees with real flower and leaf detail.
caveat: Small accents rather than continuous ornamental borders.

name: Weed Plant 02
location: Low patches between tree roots and the existing mossy rough.
fit: Broad glossy leaves break up repeated grass tufts.
caveat: Select greener variants; avoid excessive yellowing.

name: Island Tree 02
location: One windswept coastal tree behind the landing cove.
fit: Gnarled wood and green broadleaf foliage suit a rugged pirate shoreline without palms.
caveat: Scanned base needs careful burial and no overlap with rocks; optimize dense leaves.

name: Shrub 03
location: Thin pockets of meadow growth at the outer rough edge.
fit: Upright leaf shapes create a different silhouette from low grass.
caveat: Use grouped natural patches, never on the fairway or in bunkers.

name: Shrub 04
location: Small glossy-leaf clusters under tall pines.
fit: A greener middle layer between ground cover and tree canopy.
caveat: These are branch variants; cluster their bases convincingly.

name: Flower Gazania
location: A sunny pocket above the beach, beyond maintained sand.
fit: Orange daisy-like flowers add a warm accent against the green forest.
caveat: Keep the orange coverage restrained.

name: Flower Ursinia
location: Low flower patches along the inland cove boundary.
fit: Sprawling flowers give the ground a natural small-scale shape.
caveat: An alternative to Gazania, or mix lightly; not a blanket flower meadow.

name: Flower Stinkkruid
location: A few silver-green patches among coastal rocks.
fit: Small yellow blooms and softer foliage vary the coast's palette.
caveat: Grey-green leaves are less lush; reserve for the drier coast.

name: Fir Sapling
location: Young trees at forest edges and in clear gaps beneath mature trees.
fit: Mixed tree ages make the forest feel naturally grown.
caveat: Use lower-detail variants and prevent low branches blocking trails.

name: Fir Tree 01
location: A few tall canopy anchors behind the course and on distant islands.
fit: Detailed high crowns and trunks reinforce the tall-forest silhouette.
caveat: Very heavy source model; reduced geometry and texture sizes are required for mobile.

name: Tree Small 02
location: One or two broadleaf trees between pine groups.
fit: An airy green crown breaks the repeated conifer silhouette.
caveat: Heavy source model needs optimization; preserve the current forest composition.

name: Crystalline Iceplant
location: Small succulent patches where rocky land meets the beach.
fit: Low fleshy leaves make the coastal transition believable.
caveat: Coastal accent only; not a replacement for lush inland grass.

name: Namaqualand Rocks 01
location: Small mixed stones beside major shoreline boulders.
fit: Quartz-rich colour and multiple shapes reduce repeated-rock appearance.
caveat: Keep near natural size and partially bury; do not scale into enormous cliffs.

name: Tree Stump 01
location: A single mossy stump in the wild wooded edge.
fit: Scanned bark and moss add a close-up point of natural detail.
caveat: Brown litter and the scan apron need trimming or burial; keep it isolated so the floor stays green.

name: Wooden Crate 02
location: Cargo beside the barrels, between ship and chest.
fit: Rope handles and weathered timber reinforce freshly unloaded supplies.
caveat: Use one or two; keep beach approach open.

name: Wicker Basket 01
location: At the edge of the unloading pile.
fit: Natural woven fibers soften the hard timber and metal props.
caveat: One basket is enough; avoid scattering campsite clutter.

name: Ceramic Pot
location: Packed beside the supply crate.
fit: Worn earthenware reads as provisions brought ashore.
caveat: Keep it among cargo, rather than staging an established kitchen.

name: Wine Bottles 01
location: One or two bottles tucked into cargo.
fit: Dark glass catches the existing warm light and suggests ship provisions.
caveat: Modern labels need removal or replacement; keep glass shading inexpensive.

name: Wooden Axe 02
location: Resting securely against the supply crate.
fit: Weathered wood and iron fit practical exploration gear.
caveat: One tool, outside the golf and walking lanes.

name: Wooden Hammer 01
location: On a crate beside the boat.
fit: A small repair tool makes the landing feel purposeful.
caveat: Mute paint flecks if they read too modern; this is a small close-up detail.

name: Wooden Table 02
location: A small navigation station above the beach.
fit: A simple timber surface can support the existing compass and a few finds.
caveat: More established than loose cargo; use only if you want a temporary shore base.

name: Wooden Handle Saber
location: Leaning beside the chest or cannon supplies.
fit: A restrained pirate prop that ties the cargo to the ship.
caveat: Decorative only; avoid implying combat mechanics.

name: Wooden Stool 02
location: Beside the proposed navigation table.
fit: Rough handmade timber matches the grounded cove materials.
caveat: Optional companion piece; skip if the beach should feel freshly reached.

name: Wooden Bowl 02
location: Inside the cargo cluster or on the navigation table.
fit: Carved wood adds tactile detail with no modern branding.
caveat: Small decorative accent, not a field of repeated bowls.

name: Brass Pot 01
location: Packed near the barrel group.
fit: Warm aged metal complements the compass, lantern, and chest.
caveat: Keep it cargo; no active cooking scene on the beach.

name: Vintage Pocket Watch
location: Beside the compass on a single crate.
fit: An ornate little discovery object suits the exploration story.
caveat: Tiny at normal scale; best for a close-up or later inspect interaction.

name: Magnifying Glass 01
location: On the navigation crate beside the watch.
fit: Suggests studying discoveries rather than permanently settling the island.
caveat: Skip costly real-time lens refraction on mobile.

name: Modular Wooden Pier
location: One short landing section beside the ship, if desired.
fit: Worn planks, rope, and pilings match the existing Smuggler’s Cove assets.
caveat: Optional infrastructure: implies a previous visitor; use one small section and add walkable collision.

name: Brass Goblets
location: One or two beside the treasure chest.
fit: A small glint of recovered treasure strengthens the pirate theme.
caveat: Choose a couple, not a banquet; keep metal roughness naturally worn.
